newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM PRAISES EMERGENCY SERVICES OVER PROBE SCARE
The Prime Minister has praised Defence and emergency services for their handling of today's threat from a Russian space probe.
The probe, carrying 200 grams of radioactive plutonium eventually landed in the Pacific Ocean, west of Chile.
United States President, Bill Clinton, phoned Mr Howard this morning to warn that the space probe may land in northern central Australia.
Mr Howard put the Defence force on alert and Emergency Management Australia was charged with dealing with a crash landing.
The Defence and Emergency service preparations weren't needed, but Mr Howard praised the services for their advice.
Emergency Management Australia says the services worked extremely well together.
WAGE INCREASE DISPLEASES MANUFACTURERS
Employers are unhappy with the Federal Government's proposed eight dollars a week pay increase for workers on below average earnings.
The manufacturing sector says it will be hit hardest by the move, which it says will drive prices up.
Allan Handberg, of the Australian Chamber of Manufacturers, says the move's likely to discourage foreign investment.
David Edwards, from the Victorian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, has criticised the Federal Government for claiming the move is a wage increase.
Mr Edwards says it should be seen as a safety net, not a wage change, and people who've received increases over and above the award shouldn't receive any increase.
REGULAR SUNBURN LEADS TO CANCER
Researchers have found people aged between 15 and 24 who suffer regular, intensive doses of sunburn are most likely to end up with melanoma, the deadliest form of skin cancer.
The research shows people who constantly get sunburnt may double the risk of developing melanoma.
Long-term exposure to the sun was found to be less likely to lead to melanoma than regular, intensive bursts of sun.
About 35 cases of melanoma are diagnosed in the 15-to-24-year-old age group each year.
Sun Smart's Campaign Manager, Craig Sinclair, says he's hopeful sun protection habits among young people will slowly improve.
NEW SYDNEY AIRPORT A PRIORITY
Federal Labor MP, Anthony Albanese, says the Government must speed up arrangements for a new Sydney airport, following its decision to cap aircraft movements at 80 an hour at the existing airport.
Transport Minister, John Sharp this morning announced the Government will keep its promise to legislate for no more than 80 take-offs or landings an hour at the airport.
Mr Albanese had introduced a private member's bill for a limit of 80 movements an hour in a bid to force the Government to bring in the cap.
Mr Albanese welcomes the announcement but says it increases the need to fast track a second Sydney airport.
He also opposes the cap being lifted during the Sydney Olympics.
FOURTH PERSON CHARGED WITH ADELAIDE BASHING DEATH
A fourth person has been charged with murder over the weekend bashing death of an Adelaide doctor.
The 21-year-old man, from the suburb of Elizabeth North, is expected to face court this afternoon.
A youth aged 17, a 15-year-old boy and a 14-year-old girl, are facing the Youth Court today charged over the death.
52-year-old locum Dr Peter Goh failed to return from a house call on Saturday morning.
His body was found in scrub, near One Tree Hill, later in the day.
ICEBERG TRAVELLING NORTH SURPRISES SCIENTISTS
Scientists travelling back to Australia from Antarctica have passed an unusual sight.
They've encountered a large iceberg at 54 degrees south, much further north than usual.
Icebergs are usually first seen about 66 degrees south.
The Australian Antarctic Division in Hobart says the ice has been exceptionally heavy in Antarctica this year.
However, it says it can't explain what an iceberg is doing further north than usual.
MOTORBIKE SEARCH FOR FOUR MISSING MEN
Police are now searching the Brindabellas mountain range south west of Canberra on motorcycle for four men and two dogs missing since Sunday.
An 18-year old man, two men in their twenties, one 48-year old man and three dogs set out on Saturday in two four wheel drives.
Police say they are not overly concerned for the survival of the fishermen who have food, shelter and camping gear with them.
They believe the men may be trapped in country flooded by overflowing creeks and rivers.
POLICE ASSOCIATION QUIET ON CORRUPTION ACTION
The Police Association is making no comment after a call by New South Wales Police Royal Commission Justice Wood for the two police unions to detail what they've done to fight corruption.
Royal Commissioner Wood made the request after former Police Commissioner Tony Lauer said a former Police Association president had criticised his appointment in 1991.
Mr Lauer told the Commission concern had been expressed about his former role as a corruption investigator.
Police Association Secretary Phil Tunchon says the Association is consulting its solicitors about the exchange this afternoon.
